item.title: Developing a genetic toolkit for manipulating abundant intestinal microbes
item.description: Weill Cornell Medicine investigators have developed a set of molecular tools to regulate the activity of specific genes in one of the most common classes of intestinal bacteria. The ability to genetically manipulate these microbes could lead to a better understanding of the role they play in human physiology and disease. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How to win shares and influence fast-food market: Warm and fuzzy can't cut it
item.description: New research from QUT challenges a common assumption in social media marketing: For fast-food brands, social media posts that signal expertise and competence are shared more often than those focused on warmth and friendliness. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Invites Media to LunaRecycle Challenge Finale Event in Alabama
item.description: NASA will announce the winners of the final phase of its LunaRecycle Challenge on Friday, Aug. 28, at The University of Alabama (UA) Lee Styslinger College of Engineering in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. Launched in 2024, the challenge incentivizes the invention of new recycling systems that could support non-metabolic waste management efforts for future lunar missions. Media […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Lee Mohon

item.title: Even biodiversity-friendly policies may not halt declines in Europe's common birds and butterflies by 2050
item.description: As part of its efforts to map out Europe's science-policy interface for biodiversity, a paper on the correlation between governance objectives for safeguarding the biosphere and on-the-ground realities for select species groups has been published. The work is in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Machine learning method uncovers hidden patterns in DNA methylation
item.description: In a study recently published in Nature Communications, researchers from Berlin, Potsdam, and Jena present a new method for analyzing the epigenome. The machine-learning method identifies differentially methylated DNA regions without sample labels—a prerequisite for many existing algorithms. This makes it possible to identify previously hidden biological patterns as well as new subgroups of cells or diseases. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Buy now, pay later' may reshape retail prices, inventory, research finds
item.description: "Buy now, pay later" plans—which allow consumers to split purchases into a handful of interest-free installments—have become a common way for Americans to pay for everything from furniture to groceries. New research from Olin Business School at Washington University in St. Louis suggests the increasingly popular payment option can have consequences beyond the checkout screen—influencing retail prices, inventory decisions and the financial burden on consumers. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Electron beams cut poultry pathogens while preserving turkey quality
item.description: Researchers are gauging the effectiveness of electron beams in the fight against foodborne pathogens in poultry. "Impact of Electron Beam (eBeam) Treatment on Meat Quality and Sensory Attributes of Ground Chicken and Turkey" is published in the journal Poultry Science. At the heart of the study is eBeam, a nonthermal technology that uses high-energy electron beams to cause irreparable damage to pathogen DNA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Ames’ Contributions to Roman’s Mission
item.description: Set to launch on Sunday, Aug. 30, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will empower astronomers to explore vast regions of the cosmos and settle essential questions in the areas of dark energy, dark matter, planets outside our solar system, and the formation and growth of galaxies over cosmic time. Key contributions to Roman’s mission […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Gianine Figliozzi

item.title: Chemists harness light to build 3D molecular structures for drug discovery
item.description: Researchers from the Department of Chemistry at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), led by Professor Jian He and collaborators, have developed a new light-driven method for constructing three-dimensional molecular building blocks that could give medicinal chemists greater flexibility in designing new drug candidates. The approach broadens the range of starting materials that can be used while suppressing unwanted polymerization, overcoming key limitations of existing synthetic methods. The findings have been published in Nature Chemistry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Learning to lead: Navigating competing expectations helps new managers build stronger teams
item.description: Becoming a team leader doesn't just mean taking on more responsibility. It means learning to navigate competing expectations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: SpaceX announces plans for $100 billion 'spaceport' in Louisiana
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX announced plans Tuesday to build a $100 billion facility in the southern U.S. state of Louisiana to launch its anticipated Starship megarockets, currently being developed at the company's Texas Starbase. Publicado también por: CNBC - World. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using plutonium to probe the universe: Magneto‑ν experiment advances dark matter and neutrino research
item.description: Astronomers can't see dark matter directly, but they know it's there: Its gravity shapes galaxies and the large-scale structure of the cosmos. In an effort to uncover the composition of this hidden mass, a team at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) is pursuing evidence of particles that exist beyond the standard model of physics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Grassland birds are disappearing even from areas designed to protect them
item.description: Even in protected areas, birds are disappearing from America's prairies, and unpredictable weather isn't helping. That's the takeaway from a new study by researchers at Michigan State University, Oklahoma State University and the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. The study, published in the journal Ecological Applications, analyzed 16 years of bird survey data at 40 tallgrass prairie sites in western Minnesota. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New workflow helps ecologists measure how individual animals use their habitat
item.description: A researcher has developed a new, reproducible workflow that lets ecologists measure, in a standardized way, how individual animals within a species differ in their habitat use, based on GPS tracking data. The tool was developed by Dr. Elina Takola of the Department of Computational Landscape Ecology at the UFZ—Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wildfires don't just pollute the air, rain may turn its smoke into fertilizer
item.description: Wildfire smoke is usually discussed as an airborne pollutant and a threat to human health. But when smoke and rain coincide, nutrients released by burned landscapes rain back down. A new study finds that smoke-rain events can deliver large bursts of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium—three nutrients essential to life—across ecosystems in the United States. As wildfires become more frequent, these nutrient pulses could become an increasingly important and largely overlooked ecological consequence of fire. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Gamma-ray signal could be long awaited evidence for WIMPs
item.description: Dark matter is known to make up roughly 85% of all mass in the universe, as evidenced by the way galaxies spin and how galaxy clusters are held together under gravity. Yet despite decades of searching, physicists have never managed to detect the elusive substance directly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bioinspired nanoparticles deliver gene editing to lower 'bad' cholesterol
item.description: Researchers from the Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore (NUS Medicine), and Tianjin Medical University General Hospital have developed a bioinspired lipid nanoparticle (LNP) that can deliver gene-editing machinery to the liver and reduce low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, commonly known as "bad" cholesterol. The nanoparticles reduced LDL and total cholesterol by more than 20% after two doses, while showing fewer signs of inflammation and toxicity than comparator formulations. The findings were published in the Journal of Controlled Release. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists resurrect ancient proteins, offering new antibiotic leads
item.description: University of Oregon biologists have resurrected prehistoric proteins up to 160 million years old that carry natural antimicrobial properties. The revived molecules could inspire the design of new treatments for antibiotic-resistant infections, a pressing global health issue. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA’s Pandora Mission Begins Study of Exoplanets, Host Stars
item.description: Pandora, NASA’s newest exoplanet mission and the first satellite to launch through the agency’s Astrophysics Pioneers program, is now making unique observations of worlds beyond our solar system and the stars they orbit. The mission will determine the atmospheric make-up of at least 20 exoplanets, including the presence of hazes, clouds, and water. “Pandora’s data […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Lunar soil reads as a cosmic time capsule for exploding stars
item.description: When a star reaches its final stages of life, it ends in a bright, powerful explosion called a supernova and scatters material across the universe. A new study led by a University of Hawai'i at Mānoa researcher has discovered that the moon's mixed-up soil can be read as a cosmic time capsule for exploding stars. The work is published in the journal Physical Review Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Moving turtle nests to save the eggs can have hidden consequences
item.description: Moving threatened sea turtle nests to cooler, safer parts of the beach can save entire clutches from rising tides and extreme heat, but new research suggests it may have hidden consequences for the hatchlings that emerge. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
item.description: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Naked photobombing comet found in public image
item.description: Sometimes images are released before anyone realizes they have been photobombed, meaning something unexpected showed up in the background. A team of researchers found a naked photobombing comet in publicly available archival data from the Subaru Telescope, resulting not in mirth but in serious scientific discoveries. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Wartime situation': Tornado ravages French village
item.description: A tornado of rare intensity devastated a village in southern France, causing widespread destruction and leaving residents in shock Tuesday, with the mayor describing the aftermath as resembling "wartime." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rare medieval manuscript fragments reveal Guernsey's lost literary history
item.description: Seventeen medieval manuscript fragments have been identified in Guernsey with support from Kent manuscript expert Dr. David Rundle, offering an unprecedented insight into the island's literary and intellectual life during a period from which almost no such evidence has survived. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Satellite analysis tracks carbon cost of coastal erosion
item.description: From Texas to Maine, coastal wetlands and marshes are releasing more than 1.45 billion pounds (660,000 metric tons) of carbon into the ocean each year, according to new research supported by NASA. Coastal marshes, like forests and tundra, store large amounts of carbon in their plants and soil, but changes caused by storms, rising seas and human development can affect how that carbon is stored and transported. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Galaxies are like cosmic gems, each with characteristics including size and shape that make them distinct. A new gallery released today from NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes displays a collection of galactic images that showcase this variety. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: With no tall trees reaching to the sky, Alaska's North Slope tundra can look desolate—especially to outsiders from the Lower 48 who are used to in-your-face greenery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Exact calculations sharpen view of atomic nuclei
item.description: Every high-energy nuclear collision leaves behind a trail of clues about the structure of atomic nuclei. Deciphering those clues, however, depends on the accuracy of the underlying theory. Physicists at Osaka Metropolitan University have now performed a full calculation within Glauber theory, a cornerstone framework for describing high-energy nuclear collisions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can laws make social media safer for young people?
item.description: From TikTok bans and age verification requirements to media literacy lessons in schools, U.S. states are exploring a wide range of strategies to protect young people online. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chemical physicists quantitatively model electron interactions in real quantum materials
item.description: A team of scientists from Caltech and Yale University has shown for the first time how to accurately quantify an important quantum phenomenon in metals, called the Kondo effect, for specific real materials. Unlike previous approaches, which for decades have relied on simplified models to qualitatively describe the effect, the new work uses the actual atomic and electronic structures of materials to solve the problem directly. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Companies, regulators and stakeholders shape sustainability reporting, says researcher
item.description: Sustainability reporting is shaped by the social, economic and political environment in which companies operate. New research shows how corporate culture, cross-border regulatory influences and stakeholder involvement in standard-setting shape how reporting practices evolve over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Genetic evidence reveals how goosegrass colonized a newly formed volcanic island
item.description: Opportunities to directly observe how life colonizes newly formed land and how ecosystems subsequently develop are exceedingly rare. In a study published in the Journal of Plant Research, researchers at University of Tsukuba used genetic analyses to investigate the origin of Eleusine indica, a grass species found on Nishinoshima, an active volcanic island in the northwestern Pacific south of mainland Japan. Having newly emerged, the island offers a unique natural laboratory for understanding the earliest stages of biological colonization and ecosystem development. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Expert pieces together puzzle from fragments of 1,600-year-old Roman text
item.description: A Roman law expert at the University of Cincinnati edited and translated a Latin legal text he pieced together from fragments that surprisingly survived in the Egyptian sands for more than 1,600 years. What's less surprising? It's about taxes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The real reasons you procrastinate—and how to stop, according to science
item.description: Faced with a task or project, do you repeatedly tell yourself that you'll do it "tomorrow," "soon" or "after watching just a few more videos"? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Listening for extinction: Study finds areas of critical concern for northern spotted owls
item.description: Northern spotted owl populations are approaching or have already crossed functional extinction across large areas of the Pacific Northwest, a new study, published in Ecological Applications found. Researchers used artificial intelligence and advanced monitoring methods to assess long-term trends at an unprecedented scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Egypt's deserts were once home to a diverse shark community
item.description: During the Late Cretaceous period, parts of Egypt were covered in water. A new study, published in the journal Cretaceous Research, describes new evidence that this tropical sea was home to a diverse community of sharks. The study adds five new species to the region's history, found in what the authors refer to as a "shark graveyard." Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 7,000-year-old beaver bone pit reveals how Europe’s first farmers used animal fur
item.description: Near Alsleben, Germany, archaeologists have unearthed a beaver bone pit that dates back 7,000 years. This remarkable find sheds light on the early farming communities and their sophisticated practices in fur exploitation. The arrangement of the bones points to organized hunting activities. Researchers suggest that such evidence indicates that these ancient peoples crafted intricate fur clothing to adapt to their environment. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: How people treat you may shape your reputation and stabilize cooperation
item.description: When one person helps, or refuses to help, another in public, this may change not only the provider's reputation but also the recipient's. A theoretical study led by Kobe University offers a simple explanation for how cooperation in large communities becomes stable and provides insights into phenomena like the bystander effect. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Brazilians are MacGyver-ing their way around traditional markets
item.description: Life hacks are everywhere on social media—people reuse everyday materials and objects to create ingenious solutions to common problems and needs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nanoscale hairs may help gecko skin trap moisture and slow evaporation
item.description: In a dry shrubland, a gecko sprints toward shelter. Its greatest danger is not a predator, although hawks circle overhead and sand cats wait in ambush. Rather, its most pressing concern is dehydration. Its skin is paper-thin; water can evaporate from its body into the dry air more quickly than it can replenish it. Fortunately, evolution has given it an adaptation: thin, nanoscopic hairs, called setulae, that cover its body and trap moisture. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A tiny drop of water is all that's needed to find threatened frogs
item.description: New James Cook University research has used highly sensitive environmental DNA (e-DNA) techniques to find two species of threatened frogs in places they've never been seen before—and find another still struggling to recover from past disease outbreaks. The research is published in the journal Conservation Science and Practice. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Chatbots are making our writing more similar but losing the identity and personality behind it
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are making writing styles more similar without changing the overall meaning, according to an analysis of more than 880,000 texts across different writing types published in Nature Human Behaviour. The findings indicate that using LLMs could make it more difficult to identify important clues about aspects of a person's identity, personality and mental health from their language. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Left‑handed people tend to be left‑leaning voters
item.description: Political preferences are generally explained by income, age and level of education. However, our research suggests that a far more unexpected trait may also have a hand in how we vote. A survey carried out in 18 western countries has shown that left-handed people tend to identify more strongly with the political left. This finding appears to be more related to identity than biology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Families bear hidden costs of finding safety
item.description: Led by La Trobe University, the research sheds light on a largely overlooked question in response to family violence: What does it cost families to become safe? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Young golden eagles leave their parents' territory late
item.description: When a young golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) finally leaves its parents' territory, it leaves behind the only safety net it has ever known. Until now, biologists had assumed that eagles took this step as soon as they could fly well enough to survive on their own. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The hidden physics behind the shape of rose thorns
item.description: Roses are known for their thorns, the sharp structures that can sting and prickle the skin. Thorns, botanically known as prickles, are thought to discourage animals from feeding on plants and may also help climbing roses grip other vegetation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The missing plants that could transform cities for people and nature
item.description: Urban parks and public spaces need more shrubs and small trees to improve community well-being and support wildlife, University of Queensland researchers say. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: One in four NFL players could get CTE, alarming new study finds
item.description: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is a progressive brain disease linked to repeated head impacts Fuente: The Independent - World.
item.dc:creator: Erin Keller

item.title: AI financial advice can improve decisions or steer investors wrong, experiment finds
item.description: To what extent can AI improve our financial decisions or steer us in the wrong direction? Researchers at the University of Bayreuth investigated this question in a new study involving 3,700 participants and fictional investment fund savings plans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 'Now boarding' … 240,000 miles from Earth, at the moon's first airport
item.description: The moon's getting its first airport, and it's about to get busy. Within the next two decades, NASA's planned Gateway—humanity's first lunar spaceport—may become a bustling hub for Orion crew capsules, lunar landers, cargo vehicles and astronauts traveling between Earth, the moon and, eventually, destinations in the deep unknown. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Probing issues relevant to students boosts civic engagement
item.description: When social studies students delve into issues that affect their communities and discuss them in class, they are more likely to consider other people's points of view and are generally more interested in voting and other ways of participating in civic life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Shingles vaccine linked to 24% lower dementia risk
item.description: Older adults who received the Shingrix shingles vaccine were 24% less likely to be diagnosed with dementia over four years in a study of more than 500,000 people. Researchers estimate the difference could amount to roughly one dementia case prevented for every 17 people vaccinated. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Monitoring employee performance: The pitfalls for HR
item.description: Performance metrics designed to motivate employees and drive efficiency in the workplace can paradoxically leave workers less engaged and more likely to quit, research has found. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Integrating Model-Based Systems Engineering and Fault Management to Enable Autonomous Space Missions
item.description: Fully autonomous space mission operations require the ability to detect faults and compensate for them without human intervention. To address this challenge and provide model-based support for system design and operations, it is important to connect fault management (FM) and model-based systems engineering (MBSE). This approach was successfully demonstrated with the model-based generation of a […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Supercharged “natural killer” cells could be a powerful new cancer weapon
item.description: Researchers have found a way to supercharge natural killer cells, powerful immune cells that can attack cancer, so they can penetrate solid tumors and keep fighting once inside. In mice, these specially prepared tissue-resident cells slowed the growth of several tumors, including melanoma and head and neck cancers, and worked even better when paired with the antibody drug cetuximab. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Archaeologists investigate a feared young woman's 17th century vampiric grave in Poland
item.description: In 2022, excavations at a cemetery in Pień, Poland, led by researchers from the Institute of Archaeology at Nicolaus Copernicus University, led to a mysterious discovery. In what they call Grave 75, they uncovered the 400-year-old remains of a young adult woman buried in a very unusual and unsettling way. A curved iron sickle was placed directly over her neck, with its blade pointing toward her throat, while a triangular iron padlock was attached to the big toe of her left foot. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Does heavy social media use damage your family's relationship?
item.description: Children glued to their phones all day? Parents spending hours scrolling? The positive (and slightly surprising) news is that while social media may not be the most meaningful way to spend your time, it is not necessarily harmful to family life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A Manhattan-sized ice island just broke free from Greenland
item.description: A huge section of Greenland’s Petermann Glacier has snapped off, forming an ice island about the size of Manhattan. Satellites watched cracks spread rapidly before the 76-square-kilometer slab finally broke free on August 4. It is the glacier’s biggest calving event since 2012, and scientists say two even larger pieces could eventually follow. The rare Arctic iceberg will now be tracked as it drifts, breaks apart, and potentially affects shipping routes. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Moon mission delay a hiccup, but Chinese rocket city Wenchang remains on the march
item.description: For generations, Wenchang, on Hainan’s northeastern coast, was better known for coconuts, its namesake chicken and the emigrants who left for Southeast Asia in search of a living. Now the rhythms of life here have been altered, gradually and then all at once, by China’s space programme. Wenchang Space Launch Site staged its first launch in 2016. Since then it has become one of the country’s top name-cards for rocket launches. I was near the site over the weekend, excited to witness the planned... Fuente: South China Morning Post.
item.dc:creator: Wency Chen

item.title: Large mammals alter soil chemistry and increase fertility in the Atlantic Forest
item.description: A study published in the journal Ecological Monographs indicates that large mammals, such as tapirs, peccaries, agoutis and deer, alter the chemical composition of litter and soil in tropical forests of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. As a result, they increase nutrient availability and, possibly, soil fertility. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The little red dots of our cosmos might hide something big
item.description: Little red dots may reside in small, dense galaxies with total masses equivalent to around 1 billion times that of the sun, according to research published in Nature Astronomy. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ancient dental calculus reveals diverse diets of commoners in premodern Osaka, Japan, the 'Kitchen of the Realm'
item.description: What did ordinary people really eat in premodern Japan, beyond the dishes described in cookbooks and the bones discarded at urban waste pits? Reconstructing past diets at the level of individual food items is remarkably difficult. Traditional archaeological approaches and stable isotope analysis of human skeletons reveal broad dietary categories—such as reliance on marine fish and C3 plants. But they cannot show which specific taxa or tissues each person consumed, nor how access differed among social groups in a stratified society like premodern Japan. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can AI replace traditional language learning? A new study says not yet
item.description: When university students set out to learn English as an additional language, it's not just about internalizing a new list of words; they also have to learn common word combinations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: AI helps workers most when paired with experience, new study finds
item.description: As companies race to integrate artificial intelligence into the workplace, new research suggests workers benefit most when AI is paired with experience rather than treated as a replacement for it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Setting limits on phase transitions in the dark energy era
item.description: The universe is known to be expanding at an accelerating rate. Physicists typically attribute this acceleration to dark energy, a mysterious component of the universe that exerts negative pressure, causing space to expand faster. Dark energy is thought to have become the predominant influence on the universe's evolution around 3–4 billion years ago, at the beginning of what is known as the dark energy era. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study finds sustainable farming program helps refugees, immigrants boost health while launching agribusinesses
item.description: The slang term "touch grass" encourages people to step away from the internet or devices and connect with the real world. New research from the University of Kansas has found that a project that helps resettled refugees and immigrants learn sustainable farming has many of the term's same benefits, improving people's mental and physical well-being and training them to run independent agricultural businesses. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Sophie Adenot se prepara para su segunda caminata espacial desde la Estación Espacial Internacional
item.description: La astronauta francesa Sophie Adenot realizará este martes su segunda caminata espacial junto al estadounidense Anil Menon, apenas una semana después de convertirse en la primera mujer francesa en efectuar una actividad extravehicular. Durante la operación, prevista para durar unas seis horas y media, ambos reemplazarán una antena de comunicación de la Estación Espacial Internacional. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Atomic catalyst unlocks the hidden value of plant waste
item.description: Scientists have created a highly efficient catalyst that breaks down stubborn lignin from plant waste into useful chemicals under relatively mild conditions. By revealing exactly how the catalyst works at the atomic level, the discovery could help turn forestry and agricultural waste into renewable building blocks for fuels, plastics, and other materials. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Cool Japan: Human fridge chills workers in extreme heat
item.description: Feeling dizzy and unwell after cycling to work in Japan's punishing summer heat, warehouse worker Isao Tabuchi headed for his company's newest acquisition: a refrigerator for humans. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The hidden chemistry behind glow-in-the-dark art
item.description: Some of the world's brightest colors don't just reflect light; they create it. Scientists and museum conservators are now uncovering why these luminous pigments fade and how to preserve them for future generations. The findings could help protect artwork while informing the development of longer-lasting phosphorescent materials for a variety of applications, from fashion runways to airport runways. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Namibia paves way for phosphate mining in the Atlantic Ocean
item.description: Namibia has granted environmental clearance for an offshore phosphate mining project that paves the way for the world's first commercial seabed-dredging operation for the mineral, despite opposition from green groups and the fishing industry. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tides can vary by almost a meter across a single bay, four decades of satellite images reveal
item.description: Tide levels can vary by almost a meter across a single bay, according to a new study that uses decades of satellite images to measure tides at the scale of individual beaches. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Bright ideas accelerate the hunt for quantum emitters
item.description: The search for materials that can power future quantum technologies is accelerating, but identifying the most promising candidates remains painfully slow. Evaluating whether a material can efficiently emit quantum light requires computationally intensive simulations, making it difficult to screen the vast number of available materials. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Tens of thousands flee fire near U.S. city of Reno
item.description: Tens of thousands of people looked set to spend another night away from home Monday as a wind-driven fire bore down on the western U.S. city of Reno. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists find hidden “highways” guiding animal evolution
item.description: A sweeping analysis of thousands of animal genomes suggests that chromosomes do not evolve randomly but instead follow a limited number of irreversible “evolutionary highways.” These one-way genetic changes preserve clues to more than 600 million years of animal history and could even help researchers explore where evolution may head next. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Después de años escuchando lo contrario, este estudio finlandés dice que pasar mucho tiempo frente a una pantalla favorece el rendimiento cognitivo
item.description: En 2007, en la ciudad finlandesa de Kuopio, un equipo de investigadores reclutaron a poco más de 500 niños de entre 7 y 9 años. Su idea era responder a una pregunta aparentemente sencilla : ¿cuánto influye moverse en el desarrollo de los niños? Durante el estudio, midieron la actividad física, midieron la dieta y, casi de propina, preguntaron por las horas que pasaban haciendo determinadas cosas. Entre ellas, mirando pantallas. Ocho años después, cuando trataron de ver cómo iba el desarrollo cognitivo de los 260 participantes que estaban aún vinculados al proyecto, los investigadores se… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Javier Jiménez

item.title: In 2014, scientists set off 23 blasts to uncover magma hidden beneath Mount St Helens
item.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers utilized controlled explosions paired with seismic technology to investigate Mount St. Helens' subterranean magma systems. They discovered a magma-reservoir located between four to fifteen kilometers deep. This extensive analysis employed numerous instruments to track seismic waves within the volcano, yielding vital knowledge about magma movements. Such understanding is instrumental in forecasting volcanic activity and potential eruptions. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
